purpose: Evaluation framework for adaptive AI mock interviews. The rubric evaluates technical knowledge, targeted skill mastery, answer quality, communication and observable speaking behavior. It does not infer emotions, personality or confidence from appearance or voice.

scoring_scale.0: No meaningful answer or completely incorrect
scoring_scale.4: Strong understanding; correct and reasonably detailed
scoring_scale.5: Excellent understanding; accurate, complete and well-reasoned

technical_correctness.description: Accuracy of technical concepts in the answer.

score_guidelines.2: Some correct concepts but significant errors
score_guidelines.5: Highly accurate with strong technical depth

skill_mastery.description: How well the student demonstrates mastery of the targeted skill.

score_guidelines.5: Advanced demonstration of the skill with depth

relevance.description: How directly the answer addresses the question.

completeness.description: Whether important parts of the question are addressed.

reasoning.description: Ability to explain why a solution or decision is appropriate.

score_guidelines.5: Deep, structured reasoning with relevant trade-offs

clarity.description: How clearly the answer is expressed.

score_guidelines.5: Exceptionally clear and easy to follow

structure.description: Organization and logical flow of the answer.

pace.description: Observable speaking rate during the response.

score_guidelines.1: Frequently difficult to follow because of speaking rate
score_guidelines.2: Noticeably too fast or too slow in several portions
score_guidelines.5: Well-controlled speaking rate that supports clear communication

pace.note: Use only as a communication signal. Do not interpret speaking rate as intelligence, confidence, personality or technical ability.

score_guidelines.1: Frequent or unusually long pauses substantially disrupt communication
score_guidelines.5: Pauses are used naturally without disrupting communication

pauses.note: Pauses must be reported descriptively. They must not automatically be treated as negative and must not be interpreted as lack of confidence.

score_guidelines.0: Very frequent fillers substantially interfere with communication
score_guidelines.1: Frequent fillers noticeably disrupt the response
score_guidelines.3: Some filler usage but communication remains understandable
score_guidelines.5: Very low or negligible filler usage

filler_words.note: Filler-word frequency is communication feedback only. It must not be interpreted as a measure of intelligence, technical ability, confidence or personality.

score_calculation.scale: Each evaluation dimension is scored from 0 to 5.
score_calculation.technical_performance: Technical Performance = (technical_correctness × 25 + skill_mastery × 20 + relevance × 15 + completeness × 5 + reasoning × 5) / 70
score_calculation.communication_performance: Communication Performance = (clarity × 10 + structure × 8 + pace × 4 + pauses × 4 + filler_words × 4) / 30

knowledge_gap.definition: The student does not demonstrate sufficient understanding of the underlying concept or targeted skill.
signals: cannot apply the concept to a basic scenario

performance_gap.definition: The student appears to have relevant knowledge or evidence but does not demonstrate it effectively during the interview.
signals: difficulty applying knowledge despite relevant evidence
resume or project evidence exists but interview demonstration is weak

no_significant_gap.definition: The student demonstrates sufficient understanding of the targeted skill and communicates the answer effectively.

adaptive_decision_rules.reason: Student demonstrates acceptable understanding but may need deeper verification.
Student may have a knowledge gap.
Technical performance is stronger than verbal presentation.

adaptive_decision_rules.action: ask simpler targeted follow-up before classification
adaptive_decision_rules.reason: Relevant evidence exists but interview performance is weak. Additional evidence is required to distinguish a knowledge gap from a performance gap.

ai_interviewer_behavior.question_source: Questions must be selected from the approved interview question bank or generated only within the approved question schema and targeted skill constraints.
ai_interviewer_behavior.skill_targeting: Questions must directly target the student's selected skill gaps from Module 2 and the requirements of the selected target role.
adaptive_behavior: Start at an appropriate difficulty for the selected skill.
Increase difficulty after strong demonstrated performance.
Ask clarification or application questions after moderate performance.
Decrease difficulty and test fundamentals after weak performance.
Use targeted follow-ups instead of random unrelated questions.
Use previous answers to determine the next question.
Avoid repeating the same question unless verification is necessary.
Keep the interview within a configurable question/time limit.
communication_behavior: Ask one clear question at a time.
Allow the student sufficient response time.
Do not penalize accent or regional pronunciation.
Do not infer emotion from facial appearance.
Do not infer confidence from facial expressions or voice.
Do not use camera appearance as an evaluation factor.
technical_behavior: Evaluate technical correctness separately from communication quality.
Evaluate the skill selected by the student and relevant role requirements.
Use follow-up questions to verify shallow or unsupported answers.
Distinguish knowledge gaps from performance gaps using multiple signals.

safety_and_fairness: Do not infer emotion from facial appearance.
Do not claim to detect confidence from facial expressions.
Do not claim to detect confidence from voice.
Do not penalize accent or regional pronunciation.
Do not use camera-based appearance as an evaluation factor.
Do not treat pauses automatically as negative.
Do not equate speaking speed with intelligence.
Technical correctness must remain separate from communication quality.
Communication metrics must not override technical skill evaluation.
The final hiring decision must remain with the recruiter or authorized human.
